items: Jackson Bornstein, Associate, is a member of the Specialty Finance Team where he focuses on deal sourcing, execution, and structuring. Prior to this, Jackson was an Investment Banking Associate at Credit Suisse / UBS in the Financial Institutions Group, where he worked on M&A, leveraged finance, and equity capital markets transactions covering banks, consumer finance, insurance, and fintech. Jackson graduated from the University of Michigan with a BS in Computer Science.

blocks.html: During the quarter, NB Specialty Finance (“NBSF”) focused on two key areas: monetization and diversification. With valuations approaching post- Crisis tights across sectors, NBSF continued its programmatic sales of ABS securities and completed an additional securitization of whole loan collateral. This allowed us to secure cheaper fixed-rate term financing for our whole loans relative to our prior bank warehouse facility. Turning to the redeployment of that capital, NBSF remains historically selective. As the impact of tariffs on the US consumer remains uncertain in both duration and magnitude, we sought to more actively diversify our exposure from that risk factor. We closed several transactions in broadly uncorrelated sectors including receivables lending and litigation finance, which we believe highlight each robust asset coverage and in our opinion, best-in-class partners.

Credit Facility backed by Legal Fee Receivables

items: Company Description: Houston based mass tort and personal injury law firm focused on originating and monetizing large, diversified legal claim dockets.

Company Background: Company operates a hybrid model combining a high volume personal injury practice with a large mass tort referral platform. The firm sources individual claims and contributes them to leadership firms, earning contingent legal fees upon settlement. The case book includes a mix of settled, near settled, and longer dated mass torts (e.g., Purdue, Boy Scouts, LA County), alongside a steady, short duration personal injury book that generates recurring cash flow.

Opportunity: NBSF acquired a 50% interest in a senior secured, first lien loan backed by legal fee receivables from the firm’s entire case portfolio. The investment carries a high blended coupon that is paid through a contractual sweep of all legal receivables.
Deal Merits:

blocks.html: o Strong asset coverage from settled and mature cases, supplemented by stable personal injury cash flow that helps to service interest o High diversification across different cases o First lien collateral and robust lender controls; high cash yield with multiple expected paths to principal paydown or refinance
blocks.text: o Strong asset coverage from settled and mature cases, supplemented by stable personal injury cash flow that helps to service interest o High diversification across different cases o First lien collateral and robust lender controls; high cash yield with multiple expected paths to principal paydown or refinance
Equity in Litigation Claims Finance Acquisition Platform

items: Company Description: European litigation claims acquisition platform specializing in post-liability, mass claims finance.

Company Background: Founded as a European-based litigation claims acquisition platform within a New York-based investment firm, the company focuses on acquiring large volumes of consumer and corporate claims where liability has already been established by courts or regulators. The firm operates proprietary sourcing and processing infrastructure across Europe and has deployed capital across multiple cartel and consumer redress strategies with limited binary litigation risk.

Opportunity: NBSF entered into a forward flow arrangement funding claim acquisition and processing, beginning with UK motor finance discretionary commission claims. Capital is deployed selectively, with approval rights, cost shutoff rights, and exposure to multiple future strategies.
Deal Merits:

blocks.html: o Uncorrelated return profile o Asymmetric MOIC driven economics o Investment is wrapped by an insurance provider limiting downside risk o Strong control rights and flexibility to scale or pause investment depending on economics

items: Company Description: Leading enterprise cybersecurity company specializing in bot detection, fraud prevention, and digital integrity.
Company Background: The company is a scaled SaaS business serving blue chip enterprise customers across advertising and application security.

Opportunity: NBSF originated a senior secured corporate loan to refinance existing debt, structured against the company’s contracted annual recurring revenue (“ARR”), enterprise value, and cash balance, with covenant protection tied to leverage and liquidity.
Deal Merits:

blocks.html: o Market leading technology with mission critical use cases o Diversified, high quality customer base with multiyear contracts o Conservative ARR based leverage; strong enterprise value cushion Preferred Equity in Consumer Unsecured Originator
blocks.text: o Market leading technology with mission critical use cases o Diversified, high quality customer base with multiyear contracts o Conservative ARR based leverage; strong enterprise value cushion Preferred Equity in Consumer Unsecured Originator

items: Company Description: Scaled U.S. fintech platform offering consumer lending, BNPL, and digital banking products.

Company Background: Company has originated over $35bn of loans across multiple consumer verticals. Following credit card portfolio underperformance, management has pivoted toward higher margin products and balance sheet optimization.

Opportunity: NBSF has a longstanding relationship with the company and has engaged in whole loan and credit facility transactions. Building off this relationship, NBSF invested in senior preferred equity with minimum return protections, governance rights, and downside coverage through enterprise value and asset runoff.
Deal Merits:

blocks.html: o Contractual 16–20% minimum return; senior position in the equity stack o Strong investor syndicate support o Multiple exit paths including IPO or redemption o Substantial downside protection via enterprise value and loan portfolio collateral Credit Facility backed by Colombia Point-of-Sale Receivables

items: Company Description: Colombia based point of sale lender offering short- and medium-term installment financing to consumers.

Company Background: Company provides installment loans at checkout for both small tickets and larger consumer purchases. The company has scaled rapidly with strong merchant penetration, repeat customer behavior, and backing from top tier global investors.
Opportunity: NBSF participates in a first lien facility against the company’s receivables, funding short duration consumer credit with conservative advance rates and full corporate support.
Deal Merits:

blocks.html: o Unitranche warehouse structure backed by short-dated receivables o Conservative structure with significant covenant protection o Blue chip equity sponsors o Diversified merchant base

Credit Facility Refinance backed by Agricultural Receivables

items: Company Description: Fintech platform providing short term financing and payments infrastructure to global fresh produce supply chains.

Company Background: The company enables growers, distributors, and retailers to transact more efficiently by combining credit underwriting, payments, and marketplace tools. The company operates in an asset light model with financing tied to trade flows and short dated receivables.

Opportunity: NBSF originated a warehouse facility in 2021. This transaction will refinance the existing facility with a facility with shorter term, lower advance rate, higher coupon and similar financial and performance covenants.
Deal Merits:

blocks.html: o Short duration trade finance exposure o Collateral tied to essential goods with predictable demand o Embedded technology platform improves transparency and underwriting o Scalable model benefiting from growth in cross border food supply chains

items: Credit facilities, the largest exposure in the Fund, were the biggest contributors to Fund P&L due to the high coupons of those investments.

Consumer unsecured receivables were a positive contributor in the quarter. All active consumer unsecured forward flow programs have some form of first loss protection and recent consumer performance has continued to be strong.
Point of sale receivables Were the third largest contributor in the quarter. Performance for underlying loans, which are supported by high- FICO borrowers, has been in line or above expectations.
Small business receivables were the third largest contributor in the quarter. Performance for underlying loans has been in line with expectations.

Equities and warrants were a positive contributor in the quarter. P&L was primarily driven by one position, a fintech-focused bank. The positive performance was offset somewhat by underperformance by a proptech company focused on modular homebuilding experienced weakness following a softer housing market

ABS bonds were a positive contributor to P&L in the quarter. Gains were spread across most of the book, driven by security selection and tactical asset allocation decisions informed by current fundamentals and valuations.

blocks.html: The asset‑based finance (“ABF”) market in Q3 2025 remained resilient amid a mixed macroeconomic backdrop. U.S. fundamentals continued to lend support, with a still‑healthy labor market and steady consumer activity underpinning credit performance across most collateral types. While spreads were tight by historical standards, episodic bouts of volatility reinforced investor emphasis on high‑quality, shorter‑duration assets, conservative structures, and disciplined underwriting. Credit selection remained paramount as markets differentiated more clearly between seasoned, resilient platforms and lower‑quality or growth‑oriented risk.

The collapses likely stemmed from a combination of improper collateral pledging, falsified and/or misleading financials, and improper disclosures – a possible case of bad actors intentionally seeking to exploit excess capital in both public and private markets. These episodes underscore the importance of rigorous diligence and appropriate risk-pricing, but we do not suggest a systemic flaw in private credit. The NBSF platform did not have any exposure to First Brands; the NBSF Redwood Fund LP11 had a small exposure to Tricolor ABS bonds but the overall performance impact was muted due to prudent position sizing. At this time, we plan to hold the bonds in anticipation of a partial recovery.

blocks.html: Looking ahead, the outlook for ABF remains cautiously optimistic. Robust fundamentals and continued demand for collateralized exposures are expected to support performance, though tight valuations and policy uncertainty warrant selectivity and a high-quality bias. As interest rates are anticipated to decline, current yields in asset-based credit are compelling, presenting opportunities for total returns above current coupons if duration is managed effectively. Ongoing structural innovation and increased global diversification, particularly in markets with more attractive valuations, are likely to shape the next phase of growth in asset-based finance.

The Fund utilizes a subscription facility to fund investments prior to calling capital from the LPs and the impact of those borrowings are reflected in the Net IRR calculations (amounts drawn are not treated as capital contributions). An individual LP’s Net IRR will vary based on the timing of their capital transactions (including the Fund closings in which the LP participated), their fee arrangements, and the feeder to which the LPs subscribed. LPs with higher fee arrangements will experience lower performance. No individual LP received these Net IRRs.
